author: machiavelli
statement: Legal accusation channels (before the people or many judges) vent the humors that build up against citizens; where such ordinary outlets are absent, humors discharge through extraordinary modes that ruin the republic.
source_passage: quando questi omori non hanno onde sfogarsi ordinariamente, ricorrono a’ modi straordinari, che fanno rovinare tutta una republica
scope_claimed: universal ('non è cosa che faccia tanto stabile e ferma una republica, quanto...')
testability_notes: Requires: inventory of accusation/trial institutions per polity-period; event log of tumults, lynchings, faction fights; coding of whether conflicts entered legal channels. Machiavelli himself offers a 4-case comparison (Rome, Clusium, Valori, Soderini) varying channel availability.

author: machiavelli
statement: Private repression of a citizen triggers a cascade: private offense generates fear, fear seeks defense, defense recruits partisans, partisans become parties, parties ruin the city.
source_passage: perché ne nasceva offesa da privati a privati, la quale offesa genera paura; la paura cerca difesa; per la difesa si procacciano partigiani; da’ partigiani nascono le parti nelle cittadi, dalle parti la rovina di quelle
scope_claimed: general mechanism, stated as a law-like chain
testability_notes: A process-tracing claim: requires sequenced event data (offense → armed following formation → factional violence) across multiple cities. Machiavelli supplies the Coriolanus counterfactual (what would have followed a lynching) — explicitly untestable as stated.

author: machiavelli
statement: Whenever a party within a city calls in external forces, the cause is defective civic orders: no internal channel exists to vent malignant humors ordinarily.
source_passage: qualunque volta si vede che le forze estranee siano chiamate da una parte di uomini che vivono in una città, si può credere nasca da’ cattivi ordini di quella
testability_notes: Operationalizable: cross-polity dataset of foreign-intervention invitations coded against presence/absence of judicial accusation institutions. Note the inverse inference problem: Machiavelli infers institutional defect FROM intervention.

author: machiavelli
statement: Accusation before few judges is ineffective because the few act in the interest of the few; accusations must lie before many judges to be credible.
source_passage: lo accusare uno potente a otto giudici in una republica, non basta: bisogna che i giudici siano assai, perché i pochi sempre fanno a modo de’ pochi
testability_notes: Comparative-institutional claim: tribunal size vs conviction/initiation rates against powerful defendants. Florence's Otto di Guardia (8 judges) vs Roman popular judgment is Machiavelli's implied comparison — drawn from his chancery experience.

author: livy
statement: Livy's own counterfactual: by conceding a lower grain price, the senators could probably have rid themselves of the tribunate and all the rights imposed on them against their will; whether that would have been right is harder to say.
source_passage: haud tam facile dictu est, faciendumne fuerit, quam potuisse arbitror fieri, ut condicionibus laxandi annonam et tribuniciam potestatem et omnia invitis iura inposita patres demerent sibi
testability_notes: Livy treats food-price concessions as convertible into constitutional concessions. Machiavelli does NOT reproduce this counterfactual — a notable omission given his interest in the episode (see aln:a-livy-counterfactual).

author: machiavelli
statement: Works that appear pious (like feeding the hungry) can conceal the beginning of tyranny: private benefits create partisans and embolden the benefactor to corrupt the public and force the laws.
source_passage: molte volte le opere che paiono pie e da non le potere ragionevolmente dannare, diventono crudeli, e per una republica sono pericolosissime, quando le non siano a buona ora corrette
scope_claimed: 'molte volte' (frequently), framed as a standing danger of republics
testability_notes: Requires: registry of large private benefactions (food, loans, dowries, legal protection) linked to subsequent political trajectories of benefactors. Livy supplies the mechanism's data requirements precisely: who received Maelian grain, what following resulted.

author: machiavelli
statement: A well-ordered republic opens public ways to reputation (counsel and deeds for the common benefit, rewarded with honors) and closes private ways (benefits to individuals creating partisans).
source_passage: Debbe, pertanto, una republica bene ordinata aprire le vie come è detto, a chi cerca favori per vie publiche, e chiuderle a chi li cerca per vie private
testability_notes: Machiavelli maps Rome's instruments onto this design: triumphs/honors (reward public ways), accusations (sanction private ways), dictatorship (backstop when the people are blinded by 'false good'). The typology of private benefits — loans, dowries, protection from magistrates — reads as a Florentine patronage inventory, i.e. likely informed by chancery-era observation.

author: machiavelli
statement: Leaving one such private-reputation seeker unpunished is apt to ruin a republic, because after the precedent it is difficult to return to the true path.
source_passage: Ed una che di queste cose si lasci impunita, è atta a rovinare una republica; perché difficilmente con quello esemplo si riduce dipoi in la vera via
testability_notes: Precedent-effects claim: requires sequences of unpunished private aggrandizement followed by imitation. The Roman material gives the enforcement side (Maelius punished); the claim's force rests on Florentine negatives (Medici ascent) that Machiavelli leaves implicit here.

author: machiavelli
statement: Men fight first from necessity, then from ambition; desire always exceeds the power of acquiring, producing permanent discontent with what is possessed.
source_passage: qualunque volta è tolto agli uomini il combattere per necessità, combattono per ambizione; la quale è tanto potente ne’ petti umani, che mai, a qualunque grado si salgano, gli abbandona
scope_claimed: anthropological universal, attributed to 'gli antichi scrittori'
testability_notes: Machiavelli applies it as a two-stage model of plebeian demands: tribunate (necessity/security) then honors and property (ambition). The attribution to 'ancient writers' is generic — proximate sources debated in scholarship (cf. Sallust, Polybian tradition).

author: machiavelli
statement: Men value property more than honors: the nobility yielded honors to the plebs without extraordinary scandal, but defended property with such obstinacy that the plebs resorted to extraordinary means.
source_passage: la Nobilità romana sempre negli onori cede sanza scandoli straordinari alla plebe; ma come si venne alla roba fu tanta la ostinazione sua nel difenderla, che la plebe ricorse, per isfogare l’appetito suo, a quegli straordinari che di sopra si discorrono
scope_claimed: universal preference ordering ('quanto gli uomini stimano più la roba che gli onori')
testability_notes: Operationalizable within the Roman record: compare conflict intensity (duration, violence, institutional breakdown) of honor-access disputes (consulship access, Licinian-Sextian honors provisions) vs property disputes (agrarian bills). Machiavelli derives it from exactly this comparison.

author: machiavelli
statement: Making a law that looks far backward against an entrenched custom is extremely scandalous; temporizing is preferable, for delayed evil arrives later or extinguishes itself.
source_passage: a volere levar via uno disordine cresciuto in una republica, e per questo fare una legge che riguardi assai indietro, è partito male considerato
scope_claimed: general legislative-design rule (chapter title: 'come fare una legge in una republica, che riguardi assai indietro... è scandolosissimo')
testability_notes: Tension with claim:d3c28-punish-early (correct early!) is real and acknowledged by Machiavelli's own distinction: early correction of individuals vs retroactive correction of entrenched property customs.

author: machiavelli
statement: The contention over the agrarian law, reawakened by the Gracchi against adversaries whose power had doubled in the interim, destroyed Roman liberty through the Marius-Sulla and Caesar-Pompey faction wars; yet the same plebeian appetite had also checked noble ambition for three hundred years.
source_passage: questa legge stette come addormentata infino ai Gracchi; da’ quali essendo poi svegliata, rovinò al tutto la libertà romana; perché la trovò raddoppiata la potenza de’ suoi avversari
scope_claimed: single-polity macro-historical judgment with a general moral
testability_notes: The 300-year compression treats separate statutes (Cassian bill 486, Licinian-Sextian 367, Gracchan 133) as one continuous 'law' — a major abstraction; see Case C report. The Gracchan material is outside Livy I-X (addition: other-source).

author: machiavelli
statement: Well-ordered republics must keep the public treasury rich and their citizens poor.
source_passage: le republiche bene ordinate hanno a tenere ricco il publico e gli loro cittadini, poveri
testability_notes: Links Cases B and C: Maelius is the private-wealth danger realized; the agrarian failure is diagnosed as a defect in the poverty-maintaining mechanism. Requires wealth-distribution data (census classes, property registers) — the censorial census is the attested Roman instrument.

author: machiavelli
statement: When conquered fields lay far from the plebs' eyes and in places hard to cultivate, they were less desired, and the agrarian humor subsided — resurging only with the Gracchi.
source_passage: i campi che possedevano i nimici di Roma essendo discosti agli occhi della plebe, ed in luogo dove non gli era facile il cultivargli, veniva a essere meno desiderosa di quegli
scope_claimed: explanation for the law's dormancy period
testability_notes: A geographic hypothesis testable against colony enrollment data: enrollment rates vs distance from Rome. Livy's Antium datum (under-enrollment at ~50 km) is consistent, but Livy's own stated mechanism is satiety (fastidium copia), not distance — see aln:c-antium-explanation.
